title: fix panic in send command
body:
this is for [#52 ](https://github.com/cashubtc/cashu-feni/issues/52). It looks like the panic was because it was trying to access  `filteredKeySets` which was not initialized. 

also have a question on the arguments for the send command and the assumption I made. I wasn't quite sure what is expected in the `mint_id` arg since it is being converted to an int? I'm assuming the value expected is the keyset id (since that is shown in the balance) so the change will get the mint url for that keyset passed.

let me know if that is how it is intended to be used or if not, I can change it.

title: mint: simplify `AmountSplit` by iterating over amount bits
body: Seems unnecessary to involve other data types like strings or floating points here, we can just directly operate on the amount uint64 variable by iterating over all the bits and add `2**i` (expressed as shift operation `1<<i`, to avoid Math.pow) to the return list if bit i is set.

title: fixes arm and amd compatibility
body:
# Issue

Found some compatibility issues with `arm64` and `amd64`
Due to this, I have changed all int64 amounts to uint64 to prevent this "bug". 

Another solution would be reducing the `MAX_ORDER` of mints to `63` 

## Script

```go 
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"math"
)

func main() {
	pow := math.Pow(float64(2), float64(64))
	inti := int64(pow)
	fmt.Println(inti)
}

```

Casting int64 returns different results based on `GOARCH`. 


# Reproduce 

Run the script above. 

## arm64

* `GOARCH=arm64 go run main.go`

`arm64` will return `9223372036854775807`

## amd64

* `GOARCH=amd64 go run main.go`

`amd64` will return `-9223372036854775808`
